comparisons.peer_summary: Data Center net revenue increased 94% to $12.6 billion in 2024 from $6.5 billion in 2023, primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs. Operating income rose to $3.5 billion in 2024 from $1.3 billion in 2023, mainly due to higher revenue partially offset by increased R&D investment.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD report significant revenue growth in their respective strategic growth areas: Intel's 'All Other' segment grew due to Altera and Mobileye, whereas AMD's Data Center segment grew 94% driven by Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs. Both disclosures highlight that these growth areas are key drivers for their respective portfolios, though AMD's growth rate (94%) vastly outpaced Intel's 'All Other' segment growth ($78 million increase on a $5.6 billion base).

comparisons.peer_summary: Semiconductor solutions segment net revenue increased due to strong demand for AI networking products, partially offset by lower demand for broadband and server storage. Infrastructure software segment net revenue increased primarily due to contributions from VMware.
comparisons.comparison: Intel's 'All Other' segment revenue growth was driven by specific business units (Altera and Mobileye) with offsetting decreases in other non-reportable segments. Broadcom similarly details that its Semiconductor Solutions segment revenue increased due to strong demand in networking products (AI), partially offset by lower demand in broadband and server storage, illustrating a similar pattern of segmented growth and decline within broader reporting categories.

comparisons.peer_topic: QCT segment revenue drivers and EBT margin change
comparisons.peer_summary: QCT revenues in fiscal 2024 increased primarily due to higher handset revenues driven by $2.8 billion in higher chipset shipments from major OEMs and higher automotive revenues from new vehicle launches with Snapdragon products, partially offset by lower IoT revenues; QCT EBT as a percentage of revenues increased primarily due to these higher revenues.
comparisons.comparison: Intel details specific revenue increases within its 'All Other' segment driven by product demand (Mobileye EyeQ) and supply fulfillment (Altera). Similarly, Qualcomm details specific revenue drivers in its QCT segment, citing higher handset revenues due to $2.8 billion in higher chipset shipments. Both companies break down segment growth into specific volume or product-led drivers rather than just aggregate figures.
